chain.label: Elevated physiological risk from prior ICH and reduced sleep
chain.trigger: the accident pilot experienced an intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) in March 2006...had the opportunity to sleep a maximum of 9 hours...2 to 4 hours less overnight sleep than the pilot was accustomed to receiving

chain.label: FAA issued unrestricted medical certificate despite ICH history
chain.trigger: the FAA Alaska Regional Flight Surgeon reviewed the pilot's application and determined that the pilot was eligible for an unrestricted first-class airman medical certificate

caused_by.evidence: the FAA was aware that the pilot had a spontaneous ICH with intraventricular extension, persistent and obvious cognitive deficits...and a strong family history of ICH

chain.label: Pilot inhibited TAWS terrain alerts
chain.trigger: the annunciator...was likely illuminated at impact and that, therefore, the unit's visual alerts (and the GNS 530's voice and visual text pop-up TAWS alerts that it controlled) were inhibited

chain.label: Mountainous terrain (Muklung Hills) along the drift path
chain.trigger: the airplane turned east-northeast (away from its destination) towards mountainous terrain and crashed into the mountainous terrain

chain.label: Pilot's temporary unresponsiveness
chain.trigger: the probable cause of this accident was the pilot's temporary unresponsiveness for reasons that could not be established from the available information

caused_by.evidence: a medical condition leading to transient incapacitation or impairment could explain the circumstances of this accident

chain.label: Unnoticed drift toward rising terrain
chain.trigger: the heading of the airplane at impact suggests that the pilot was largely unaware that the airplane was approaching the rising terrain

caused_by.evidence: this apparent lack of awareness suggests that the accident pilot's perceptions and/or responses became substantially impaired at some point after the airplane's last known Sky Connect position

chain.label: Radar altimeter alert sounds seconds before impact
chain.trigger: the estimated elapsed time from the activation of the radar altimeter's annunciator light and aural tone to the time of impact was about 4 to 6 seconds

caused_by.evidence: the airplane was in a climbing left turn when it collided with terrain
impacted mountainous, tree-covered terrain about 10 nautical miles northeast of Aleknagik
had the pilot not inhibited the TAWS's aural voice and pop-up text alerts, the system would have provided an aural and visual alert up to 30 seconds before the impending collision

chain.label: Belated aggressive control inputs before impact
chain.trigger: flight control inputs occurred shortly before terrain impact

caused_by.evidence: the radar altimeter system provided both aural and visual altitude alerts about 4 to 6 seconds before impact, which likely prompted the pilot to take aggressive action on the flight controls, resulting in the airplane nose-up pitch and left-bank angles

chain.label: Collision with mountainous terrain
chain.trigger: impacted mountainous, tree-covered terrain about 10 nautical miles northeast of Aleknagik, Alaska

caused_by.evidence: the airplane was in a climbing left turn when it impacted terrain and that flight control inputs occurred shortly before terrain impact

chain.label: Fatal and serious injuries to occupants
chain.trigger: The airline transport pilot and four passengers received fatal injuries, and four passengers received serious injuries

caused_by.evidence: the airplane sustained substantial damage, including deformation and breaching of the fuselage
